newsitem.title: POLAND: REMARKS ON RUSSIAN PENETRATION SPARK ROW IN POLAND.
newsitem.headline: REMARKS ON RUSSIAN PENETRATION SPARK ROW IN POLAND.

text.p: A political row has erupted in Poland following the Polish security minister's statements that Russian secret services were increasing their activity among the country's leadership structures.

Just before leaving for talks with German intelligence chiefs Zbigniew Siemiatkowski reiterated his remarks contained in a Saturday interview that Russian intelligence was trying to impede Poland's admission to NATO and the European Union.
"Russia, through agents of influence among politicians and businessmen, wants to block Poland's entry into the EU and NATO," he had told the heavy-weight daily Rzeczpospolita.
"Polish counter-intelligence sees increased contacts of Russian diplomats with...(Polish) politicians," he had said.
He added the contacts were both with officials from the ruling coalition of the post-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and Peasant Party (PSL) as well as with the opposition.
The opposition centrist Freedom Union party (UW) on Sunday demanded that Siemiatkowski explain his remarks before parliament.

"Sensations are usually the stock in trade of journalists, not ministers," PAP reported UW parliamentary leader Bronislaw Geremek as saying. He added that Siemiatkowski had not backed up his remarks with any evidence.
Janusz Piechocinski of the SLD's junior coalition partner PSL said in a radio discussion on Sunday that Siemiatkowski's statements could harm Poland's international interests.
Siemiatkowski's words also prompted the right-wing Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) to demand the sacking of all public officials and activists with links to Russian special services.
